investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T15:56–16:04Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion on the kata peer-pods VM resource, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this infrastructure condition: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1764 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers pod scheduling, and that scheduling fails before any evidence can be written.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or previously scheduled remote-agent pods are holding the resource and none have been released, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods.
[Likely] A surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) exhausted the finite VM slot pool on the 2 kata-capable nodes before this eval's pods could be scheduled.

[Possible] One or both kata-capable nodes became NotReady, cordoned, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reduced (e.g., node drain, resource quota change, or peer-pod provider limit), shrinking available capacity to zero.

[Possible] The 4 non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch that permanently excludes them from remote-agent pods; if the cluster was recently reconfigured (node labels changed, affinity rules tightened), the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk.

[Lower likelihood] A peer-pod provider quota at the cloud/hypervisor layer (e.g., VM instance quota) was hit, causing the kata runtime to report the resource as exhausted even if Kubernetes node capacity appears non-zero.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T15:56–16:04Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion on the kata peer-pods VM resource, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this infrastructure condition: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1764 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers pod scheduling, and that scheduling fails before any evidence can be written.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or previously scheduled remote-agent pods are holding the resource and none have been released, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods.
[Likely] A surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) exhausted the finite VM slot pool on the 2 kata-capable nodes before this eval's pods could be scheduled.

[Possible] One or both kata-capable nodes became NotReady, cordoned, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reduced (e.g., node drain, resource quota change, or peer-pod provider limit), shrinking available capacity to zero.

[Possible] The 4 non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch that permanently excludes them from remote-agent pods; if the cluster was recently reconfigured (node labels changed, affinity rules tightened), the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk.

[Lower likelihood] A peer-pod provider quota at the cloud/hypervisor layer (e.g., VM instance quota) was hit, causing the kata runtime to report the resource as exhausted even if Kubernetes node capacity appears non-zero.
